text: What Holmes tells in the weighing enclosure
why: Holmes has just promised 'Certainly, Colonel, you shall know everything' and is leading the party to the horse in the weighing enclosure, so a later explanation from him is a reasonable expectation.
Holmes himself names spirits of wine in paragraph 202 as the thing to wash the horse's face and leg with.

The story so far shows the racing horse has no white hair, although the Colonel's horse is known for its white forehead and mottled leg, and Holmes says washing will reveal it is the same horse. That points to a disguise without naming the method.

text: Race day: in the weighing enclosure, after the race
why: The race has just finished (Silver Blaze won) and the party is going round to the weighing enclosure, which is where the label places the scene.
